_about: How grade.py turns findings into the overall tier. Data, not code: change these values through the Learn step (record_feedback.py logs why). The tier is the highest level whose rule is met. Manipulation (hidden prompts) and paraphraser evidence are reported separately: they are serious, but they are not evidence that an AI wrote the text.
_style_note: The style score counts as moderate evidence only if its validated AUROC (calibration.json) reaches min_style_auroc; otherwise it is weak context at most.

web._note: A web tool flags the document when chunks holding at least flag_share of the words score >= 0.5. Two validated tools flagging, plus one non-statistical line (artefacts, references, reading, baseline), make it strong. A tool counts only if its scanned chunks cover at least min_coverage of the text.

combined._note: Calibrated combination of web detectors across splits (evidence.py). Moderate needs the document to be at least moderate_times more likely under AI, with at least min_good_tools tools that reached good_auroc on known texts among those counted. At most counter_times is reported as counter-evidence. Never strong on its own. passage_times: a single passage at or above this (stricter than the document bar, since several passages are tested) also gives moderate, worded as localised evidence.
